options.explanation: The one-hundred-and-eighty-day period applies only to a One Person Company, not to private companies generally.

questions.topic: Ch 9 · Case: books, re-opening and revision in one company
questions.case: Meghdoot Infratech Limited has its registered office at Pune and keeps its books of account in electronic mode. Part of its financial information is maintained at an office outside India. On 6 July 2027 its Board resolves to keep the books at a shared services centre at Coimbatore. The company is in its financial year 2027-28. In June 2027 the Central Government applied to the Tribunal alleging that the accounts of certain earlier financial years were prepared in a fraudulent manner. In July 2027 the directors discovered that the Board's report for the financial year 2024-25 omitted the Directors' Responsibility Statement altogether.

readLink.label: Read: Reopening and revision — ss. 130 and 131 →

questions.stem: Which statement about the inspection of Meghdoot Infratech Limited's books is correct?
questions.sourceRef: Companies Act 2013, s. 128(3)

options.text: Any member of the company may inspect the books at the registered office during business hours
options.explanation: Section 128(3) confers the right on directors, not on members.

options.text: Any director may inspect the books at the registered office, or at the other place in India where they are kept, during business hours; and where financial information is maintained outside India, copies of it must be maintained and produced for his inspection on the prescribed conditions
options.explanation: Correct. That is section 128(3), and it covers both the books kept within India and copies of information maintained outside it.

options.text: Only the members of the audit committee may inspect the books of account
options.explanation: No such restriction appears in section 128(3); the right belongs to any director.

options.text: A director may inspect the books only through an agent authorised in writing by the Board
options.explanation: The right is the director's own and is not exercised through an agent under this sub-section.

questions.stem: The earliest financial year in respect of which the Tribunal may order the re-opening of Meghdoot Infratech Limited's books of account is:
questions.sourceRef: Companies Act 2013, s. 130(3) — eight financial years immediately preceding the current financial year

options.explanation: That is nine financial years back — the off-by-one produced by counting the current year 2027-28 as one of the eight.

Correct. The eight financial years immediately preceding 2027-28 run from 2026-27 back to 2019-20, so 2019-20 is the earliest year that may be re-opened, unless a direction under section 128(5) had required the books to be kept for longer.
That is only seven financial years back; the count stops one year short.
That is six financial years back, well inside the statutory reach.

questions.stem: In relation to the Board's report for the financial year 2024-25, which omitted the Directors' Responsibility Statement:
questions.sourceRef: Companies Act 2013, s. 131(1) and its proviso

options.text: It may be revised by a resolution of the Board alone, section 131 requiring no external approval
options.explanation: Section 131 requires the approval of the Tribunal on an application made by the company.

options.text: It may not be revised at all, section 131 permitting revision only of the financial statement and not of the Board's report
options.explanation: Section 131 expressly covers the report of the Board as well as the financial statement.

options.text: It may be revised with the approval of the Tribunal, the year being within the three preceding financial years, not more than once in a financial year, with the detailed reasons for the revision disclosed in the Board's report of the year in which the revision is made
options.explanation: Correct. 2024-25 lies within the three financial years preceding 2027-28, and all three conditions — Tribunal approval, once a year, and disclosure of detailed reasons — apply.

options.text: It may be revised only with the approval of the Central Government, the Tribunal having no jurisdiction over a Board's report
options.explanation: The Central Government merely receives notice of the application under section 131; the approving authority is the Tribunal.
